text:
Flash cards of flash memory? No, this is about SSDs. They store data in NAND flash cells, and TLC (triple-level cell) flash, the everyday type in most drives, is good for roughly 3,000 write cycles per cell before it starts to wear out. That sounds limited, but the drive has ways of stretching it.

Wear leveling spreads writes evenly across every block, so no single cell gets overworked while its neighbors sit idle. Over-provisioning, typically around 7%, sets aside spare flash that the controller uses to replace worn blocks and keep performance steady.

Together, these let those 3,000 cycles last through years of everyday use, so the drive can keep handling your photos, games, and work files. Pretty good engineering, honestly.
